member.summary: Walks the AST to validate schema-aware constructs against the registered . Raises XPST0008 when a schema-element(Name) or schema-attribute(Name) references a declaration that is not in scope.
member.remarks: This checker is invoked when a schema provider is registered (which is the default — every ships with a unless the caller explicitly passes null). member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Analysis.StaticAnalyzer._resolvedModuleFiles

Keyed on the resolved file path so that multiple module files sharing the same target namespace (e.g. impl1.xqm and impl2.xqm both module namespace impl = "...") each get loaded once and merged. member.summary: Injects function and variable declarations from imported modules into the main module's declarations list so the optimizer creates physical operators for them.

Rewrites a decimal-format name to its EQName Q{uri}local form using the imported module's prolog namespace bindings, so the format key matches what prefix resolution inside the imported function's body will produce at lookup time. A null/empty name (the default decimal-format) is left null — default decimal-formats from imported modules are intentionally not propagated (the importing module's default wins).

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryFunction.MinArity
member.summary: Minimum arity for variadic functions — the fewest arguments a call may supply. Defaults to (the full parameter count), which preserves resolution for non-variadic functions and for true-variadic functions whose declared parameters are all required (e.g. fn:concat, min 2). Functions with optional trailing arguments (e.g. array:slice, fn:slice, fn:highest, map:build) override this to the count of required leading parameters so calls resolve across their whole arity range — not just at . Occurrence indicators cannot be used to infer this: fn:concat declares its parameters as item()* yet still requires two arguments.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryFunction.MaxArity
member.summary: Maximum arity for variadic functions. Defaults to int.MaxValue (unbounded). Override to set an upper bound (e.g., function-available accepts 1-2 args).

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.SourceLocation
member.summary: Source location for error reporting and debugging.

remarks.para: identifies the originating stylesheet/query module — the value of xml:base or the system-id of the source file. It's the diagnostic anchor users need when an error fires inside an imported/included module: without it, callers only see a line/column number but can't tell which file the error came from.

is populated by callers that have a base URI in hand (e.g. the XSLT parser via XElement.BaseUri); older callers that don't set it leave it null and the formatter falls back to the bare line/column form.

para.b: Coordinate conventions (Phase D8 of the source-location audit):

item.description: is 1-based in all contexts (matching System.Xml.IXmlLineInfo and ANTLR-runtime conventions).

is 1-based for XSLT-shifted file-absolute positions (set by the XSLT StylesheetParser shift helpers from IXmlLineInfo.LinePosition) and 0-based for raw ANTLR-only contexts (XQuery-direct parses where no shift was applied). Consumers that need a single convention should check the presence of to distinguish: file-absolute (Module set) → 1-based; XPath-relative (Module null) → 0-based. LSP adapters should normalize to 0-based UTF-16.

/ are 0-based character offsets into the parsed input string (XPath text). They remain input-string-relative even after location shifts. is inclusive (matches ANTLR's StopIndex): the character at EndIndex is the last character of the token range.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XdmSequenceType
member.summary: Represents an XQuery sequence type, combining an with an indicator to describe the type and cardinality of an XDM value.

remarks.para: Sequence types are the core of XQuery's type system. They appear in function signatures (function($x as xs:string) as xs:boolean), variable declarations (let $x as xs:integer := 42), and instance of / treat as / cast as expressions.

A sequence type has two parts:
— the type of each item (e.g., xs:string, element(), item()).
— the cardinality indicator: exactly one (no indicator), ? (zero or one), * (zero or more), or + (one or more).
Common pre-built instances are available as static properties (e.g., , , ).

member.summary:
Namespace URI and local name of a SCHEMA-DEFINED simple type used as a cast as / castable as target — a type an imported schema declares, as opposed to one of the built-in XSD types enumerates.
Held as plain strings rather than in because that is an Xdm.XdmTypeName, whose namespace is a NamespaceId from a fixed registry and cannot represent an arbitrary schema target namespace.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XdmSequenceType.ToString
member.summary: Renders the type in XQuery source syntax — xs:nonNegativeInteger, not the CLR enum name Integer.
member.remarks: Every diagnostic that interpolates a sequence type flows through here, so rendering the enum member made errors name a type the user had not written: declaring $n as xs:nonNegativeInteger and passing 2 reported "does not match parameterized type Integer" — wrong on all three counts. It is not parameterized, the declared type is not xs:integer, and the mismatch is precisely the derived/base distinction the word "Integer" erases. That message cost an investigation into behaviour that was correct.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Execution.InMemoryUpdatableNodeStore
member.summary: In-memory implementation of for XQuery Update Facility. Wraps XDM nodes and maintains mutable children/attribute lists to support insert, delete, replace, rename, and value-of operations.

remarks.para: Because XDM node types use required init properties for and , this store maintains a parallel mutable structure () that shadows the original immutable lists when mutations occur.

This implementation is designed for the copy/modify/return (transform) pattern where nodes are deep-copied into this store, mutated via PUL application, and then returned as results. It can also be used for standalone update execution against in-memory documents.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Execution.OrderedXdmMap
member.summary: An XDM map with guaranteed entry/insertion-order iteration, per XPath 4.0 (XQuery 4.0 / XSLT 4.0). XPath 3.1 left map order unspecified; 4.0 makes it a contract. This type makes the ordering a structural invariant rather than an incidental property of enumeration (which the BCL documents as undefined).

remarks.para: Ordering rules (XPath 4.0 §17.1):

list.item: A newly added key is appended after all existing keys.
Assigning a value to an existing key updates the value and keeps the key in its original position.
A removed-then-reinserted key is a new insertion — it moves to the end.

remarks.para: Implements so every existing consumer that pattern-matches IDictionary<object, object?> works unchanged. Key equality uses the supplied comparer (normally ) so cross-type XDM key matches behave as in op:same-key; the original key object is retained on value update, matching semantics.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Execution.AxisNavigationOperator.MakeNamespaceNode(PhoenixmlDb.Xdm.Nodes.XdmElement,System.String,System.String,System.UInt64@)
member.summary: Builds one namespace node for with a distinct synthetic identity so that a set of namespace nodes on the same element survive document-order deduplication (which keys on (TreeOrdinal, NodeId)). The parent element's groups the node with its tree; the per-element index (with a high marker bit) makes each id unique and out of range of any stored node id.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Execution.AxisNavigationOperator.GatherInScopeNamespaces(PhoenixmlDb.Xdm.Nodes.XdmElement,System.Func{PhoenixmlDb.Core.NodeId,PhoenixmlDb.Xdm.Nodes.XdmNode})
member.summary: Gathers the in-scope namespace bindings of — its own declarations plus every binding inherited from an ancestor (XDM §6.2), excluding the implicit xml binding (callers add it). Bindings are yielded nearest-first, deduplicated by prefix (nearest wins), honouring xmlns="" default undeclarations and the copy-namespaces no-inherit marker. This is the single source of truth shared by the namespace:: axis and fn:in-scope-prefixes, so the two can never disagree.
member.param: The element whose in-scope namespaces are wanted.

Resolves an ancestor by node id. Both callers pass the main node store (context.NodeStore.GetNode) so the axis and fn:in-scope-prefixes walk the same tree. Prefer this over a supplementary-provider-aware loader such as QueryExecutionContext.LoadNode: per-store s are small integers that collide across independently-parsed trees, so a loader that consults a pushed supplementary provider first could resolve an ancestor id to an unrelated node from another store and skew the walk.

True when is the same as or derived-by-restriction from in the XSD string-type hierarchy. The hierarchy:
string → normalizedString → token → language
string → normalizedString → token → NMTOKEN
string → normalizedString → token → Name → NCName → ID/IDREF/ENTITY

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Execution.QueryEngine
member.summary: Main query execution engine that orchestrates parsing, analysis, optimization, and execution.

remarks.para: is the primary entry point for compiling and executing XQuery expressions against PhoenixmlDb storage or any custom data source. Create a single engine instance and reuse it across queries — the engine itself is stateless and thread-safe. Each query execution creates its own internally, so concurrent queries do not interfere with each other.

The engine supports three execution patterns:
— streams results one at a time via IAsyncEnumerable, ideal for large result sets.
— materializes all results into a list, convenient for small result sets.
— returns only the first result (or null), useful for aggregations and existence checks.
For advanced scenarios, call to pre-compile a query and inspect the before executing it.

Constructor parameters inject optional providers for node access (), document metadata (), and URI-based document resolution (). When using the built-in PhoenixmlDb storage layer, these are supplied automatically; implement them only when integrating a custom data source.

example.para: Cross-document join using a document resolver:

member.summary: Creates a new with optional providers for node access, metadata, and document resolution.
member.param: Optional query plan optimizer for database-layer optimizations (e.g. index scans). When null, no external optimizations are applied.
Custom function library. Defaults to which includes all XQuery 3.1 built-in functions.
Resolves values to XDM nodes. Required for queries over stored documents.
Resolves document-level metadata (e.g., custom properties stored alongside XML).
Resolves URIs for fn:doc() and fn:collection(). Required for cross-document queries.

Schema provider for schema-aware processing. Defaults to a fresh with no schemas loaded — callers can call ImportSchema on it, or pass a custom implementation (RelaxNG, Schematron-derived, in-memory, etc.). Pass null to disable schema features entirely (rare; primarily for size-constrained embedded scenarios).

Consulted by the static analyzer when an import module declaration cannot be resolved from its location hints (or are absent). member.summary: Container statistics consulted by the cost-based optimizer to score plan alternatives (e.g. index lookup vs. scan). When null, the optimizer uses (zero-knowledge constants). Hosts with live data (a database engine) should supply a real adapter so the index-vs-scan crossover reflects the container's actual node count — otherwise even highly selective predicates can be scored against the 100k-node default and lose to a scan.

member.summary: Maximum recursion depth for tree traversal and function calls. Prevents stack overflow on deep or cyclic structures.

remarks.para: This is a security boundary that protects against denial-of-service via deeply recursive queries. The default of 1,000 is sufficient for virtually all real-world queries. Queries that exceed this limit are terminated with error FOER0000.

To allow deeper recursion (e.g., for mathematical computations), increase this value. Note that very deep recursion also increases memory usage and execution time. A future optimization (tail-call elimination) may remove this limit for tail-recursive functions.

Prolog-declared namespaces only become in-scope on an element if they are USED (as an element or attribute prefix).

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Execution.QueryExecutionContext.CurrentLocation
member.summary: The source location of the AST node currently being evaluated, or null when no operator has installed one. Pushed via .

remarks.para: Used by and to auto-attach module/line/column to runtime exceptions, so consumers (LSP, diagnostic UIs, log readers) get actionable error locations without each raise site having to thread by hand.

Operators install their AST node's location around their core evaluation — using var _ = context.PushLocation(this.Location); — so any exception that fires from the operator's body (or a function it calls) inherits the closest known location. Null pushes are no-ops, so operators with no location info (synthetic / generated) leave the prior location in place.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Execution.QueryExecutionContext.PushLocation(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.SourceLocation)
member.summary: Pushes as the current source location for the duration of the returned scope. Disposing the scope restores the previous location. A null push leaves the prior location unchanged so callers don't need to null-check before pushing.
member.param: The location to install, or null to keep the current one.
member.returns: A stack-allocated scope; dispose (via using) to restore.

example.code: using var _ = context.PushLocation(this.Location); // any exception raised below auto-picks up `this.Location`

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Execution.XQueryRuntimeException
member.summary: Exception thrown when an XQuery expression fails during execution (as opposed to during parsing or static analysis).

remarks.para: Runtime exceptions correspond to XQuery dynamic errors defined in the XQuery 3.1 specification. The property contains a standard XQuery error code (e.g., "XPDY0002", "FOER0000", "FORG0006") that identifies the error category.

Common error codes:
XPDY0002 — Context item is undefined (e.g., using . without a context).
XPST0008 — Unbound variable reference.
FORG0006 — Invalid argument type (e.g., effective boolean value of a map).
FOER0000 — Unidentified error, including execution limit violations.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Execution.XQueryRuntimeException.ErrorCode
member.summary: The XQuery error code (e.g., "XPDY0002", "FOER0000") identifying the error category as defined by the XQuery 3.1 and XPath 3.1 specifications.

Distinct from the zero-arity below, which CONSTRUCTS an empty array. Same name, different arity and meaning — the predicate was missing, so array:empty($a) resolved to nothing and reported "Unknown function: empty#1" even though a class called ArrayEmptyFunction existed.
Found by Dimitre Novatchev's Generators library, which calls the predicate three times.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryException
member.summary: Exception thrown by the XQuery fn:error() function or when a built-in function encounters an error condition defined by the XQuery and XPath Functions and Operators specification.

remarks.para: This is the base exception type for errors raised by XQuery built-in functions (e.g., type conversion failures, invalid arguments). It is distinct from , which covers dynamic errors raised by the execution engine itself (e.g., unbound variables, context errors).
The follows the standard XQuery error code format (e.g., "FOTY0013" for atomization of function items, "FOER0000" for fn:error() with no arguments).

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryException.ErrorCode
member.summary: The XQuery error code (e.g., "FOTY0013", "FOER0000") identifying the error as defined by the XQuery and XPath Functions and Operators specification.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryException.ErrorNamespaceUri
member.summary: Namespace URI of the error code QName. Null for built-in errors (which live in the default err: namespace, http://www.w3.org/2005/xqt-errors).

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryException.ErrorPrefix
member.summary: Prefix of the error QName (e.g., "example" for example:EXER3141). Null for built-in errors.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryException.ErrorValue
member.summary: The error value passed as the third argument to fn:error($code, $description, $error-object). Null when no error object was provided.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryException.Module
member.summary: The originating module URI (file path or system id), if known. Populated for errors that fire from an executor with a in hand.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryException.Line
member.summary: 1-based line number in the originating module, or null if not known.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryException.Column
member.summary: Column number in the originating module, or null if not known. 1-based for XSLT-shifted file-absolute positions; 0-based for raw ANTLR-only (XQuery-direct) contexts. See remarks for the full convention.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryException.RelatedLocations
member.summary: Phase D7 source-location-audit: secondary locations related to this error, e.g. the position of a specific input that triggered a type assertion. Empty when the error is purely localized at the stylesheet position (most common case). LSP adapters surface these as "related diagnostics" alongside the primary // location, so users can jump from the assertion site to the data position that violated it.

member.summary: Parses a lexical date/time form, raising FORG0001 rather than a raw .NET FormatException.
member.remarks: Casting an invalid lexical form is FORG0001 per XPath 3.1 §19.1. DateTimeOffset.Parse throws FormatException, which surfaced as a .NET message with no error code — the same "error names the wrong thing" fault as the XPTY0004 it sits beside. It became easy to hit once untyped node arguments started reaching this arm: format-time(@dateTimeAttr, ...) SHOULD fail, because a dateTime lexical form is not a valid xs:time, and it should say so as FORG0001.

member.summary: Converts JSON strings to XDM document trees using the XPath functions namespace.

Creates a fn:string element. - escape=false: text = decoded value with XML-invalid chars replaced (or fallback called). - escape=true: text = raw JSON content with only \\" and \\/ decoded; add escaped="true" if has retained sequences.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.JsonToXmlConverter.ProcessEscapeTrue(System.String,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: Process a raw JSON string inner content (without outer quotes) for escape=true mode. Returns (processed text, hasRetainedEscapes). Only \" → " and \/ → / are decoded; all other sequences (\\, \r, \t, \n, \b, \f, \uXXXX) are kept.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.JsonToXmlConverter.TryDecodeSentinelEscapeTrue(System.String,System.Int32,System.String@,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: Checks if the 30 chars starting at 'pos' in 'inner' form 4 sentinel-digit \uXXXX sequences followed by \uE011 (6 chars). If so, decodes to the original 4-char hex string. The full sentinel is: \uE010 (already consumed) + 4×\uE0XY + \uE011 = 5×6 = 30 chars from pos.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.JsonToXmlConverter.ProcessJsonKeyForEscape(System.String,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary:
For escape=true mode: determine what key value and escaped-key flag to use. The key is the decoded property name from System.Text.Json (which already decoded \\uXXXX). We need the original raw key to determine if it had escape sequences. Since System.Text.Json gives us only the decoded name, we re-examine by looking for escape sequences in the raw JSON.
Strategy: the prop.Name from JsonElement is already decoded. We need to check if the raw JSON key had any backslash sequences (other than \" and \/). We use GetRawText equivalent: for object properties, we re-parse the raw JSON key from the property's raw representation.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.JsonToXmlConverter.ApplyFallbackToString(System.String,System.Func{System.String,System.Threading.Tasks.Task{System.String}},PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: Apply fallback function to each invalid character in the string. The fallback is called with the original escape sequence (e.g. "\uDEAD") or the invalid char's \uXXXX form (e.g. "\u000C" for form-feed). Lone surrogates appear as PUA sentinel sequences (U+E000 + 4×encoded-digit + U+E011) because ReplaceLoneSurrogates was called with useSentinel=true.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.JsonToXmlConverter.ReplaceXmlInvalidChars(System.String,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: Replace characters that are invalid in XML 1.0 with U+FFFD. Called when escape=false and no fallback is provided.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.JsonToXmlConverter.ReplaceLoneSurrogates(System.String,System.Boolean,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: Replaces lone surrogate escape sequences (\uDxxx without a valid pair) in a JSON string so System.Text.Json can parse it. Called for escape=false mode only. When useSentinel=false: replace with \uFFFD (replacement character, no fallback). When useSentinel=true: replace with a PUA-encoded sentinel sequence so the original codepoint can be recovered when calling the fallback function.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.JsonToXmlConverter.AppendSurrogateAsSentinel(System.Text.StringBuilder,System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Char},PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: Appends a PUA-encoded surrogate sentinel to the JSON replacement. The sentinel is a JSON escape sequence that represents 6 chars: U+E000, encoded-digit-1, encoded-digit-2, encoded-digit-3, encoded-digit-4, U+E011 which after JSON parsing becomes the 6-char sentinel in the decoded string.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XPathRound
member.summary: XPath fn:round semantics: round half towards positive infinity. For non-negative values, AwayFromZero is identical. For negative values, AwayFromZero is correct for all non-midpoint cases (e.g., -13.65 → -13.7 correctly) but rounds the wrong direction at exact midpoints (e.g., -2.5 → -3 instead of -2). We use AwayFromZero then fix exact midpoints by checking the distance from the rounded result.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.RoundHalfToEven2Function.RoundDouble(System.Double,System.Int32,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: Rounds a double half-to-even at the given decimal precision, deciding ties from the double's ACTUAL binary value rather than from its shortest decimal spelling.
member.remarks:
This used Math.Round(val, precision, MidpointRounding.ToEven). .NET's double overload applies a decimal-style correction, which manufactures ties that do not exist in binary:
round-half-to-even(250.0250e0, 2) gave 250.02, must be 250.03
The nearest double to 250.025 is 250.025000000000005684341886080801486968994140625 — strictly ABOVE the midpoint, so it is not a tie at all and rounds up. Math.Round saw a "250.025" and applied half-to-even to a tie the value does not have. The sibling cases happen to come out right for the same wrong reason: 150.015 as a double is BELOW its midpoint and 180.018 above, so decimal-thinking and binary agree there. Exactly the distinction w3c/xslt30-test issue 79 corrected in 2024 (test math-3303), which was invisible here until the XSLT runner stopped passing <assert> unconditionally.
A double is mantissa x 2^exp exactly, so |val| x 10^p is the exact rational N/D below. Rounding it is then integer arithmetic: compare 2r against D — greater rounds up, less rounds down, and only EQUAL is a genuine tie, where half-to-even applies. No binary floating point is involved in the decision, so no spurious tie can arise.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.ValueDistinctnessHelper
member.summary:
Shared basis for fn:all-equal, fn:all-different and fn:duplicate-values (XPath 4.0). The spec defines all three in terms of the same value equality as fn:distinct-values, so all three delegate to rather than each inventing a comparison of its own.
Each previously compared .ToString() of the atomized value, with two consequences. No collation could be honoured, so the arity-2 forms the spec requires did not exist at all. And values of DIFFERENT types compared equal whenever their lexical forms matched, so all-equal((1, "1")) was true and all-different((1, "1")) was false — both backwards. The comparer keeps strings under the requested collation and numerics under numeric promotion, leaving 1 and "1" correctly distinct.
Found by auditing the collation-taking functions after Martin Honnen reported the same class of defect in fn:highest/fn:lowest on 2026-08-23. None of these three had any tests.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.HighestLowestHelper
member.summary:
Shared implementation of fn:highest and fn:lowest (XPath 4.0 §14.5).
fn:highest($input as item()*, $collation as xs:string? := fn:default-collation(), $key as (fn(item()) as xs:anyAtomicType*)? := fn:data#1) as item()*
The COLLATION is the second argument and the key function the third. This engine previously declared arity 1-2 with the key second, so highest#3 did not exist and highest($seq, $key) bound a key function into the collation position — reported by Martin Honnen, 2026-08-23.
The old implementation also coerced every key with Convert.ToDouble, so highest(("apple","banana")) threw an unhandled System.FormatException and killed the process rather than raising an XQuery error. Keys now go through the same machinery fn:sort uses — CallableCoercion for the key, DataFunction.Atomize for its values, and SortHelper.CompareKeySequences for the comparison — so strings, dates and mixed numerics all order correctly and under the requested collation.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.PartitionFunction
member.summary: fn:partition($input as item()*, $split as function(item()*, item()) as xs:boolean) as array(item())*
member.remarks:
XPath 4.0 §fn:partition. $split takes TWO arguments — the partition accumulated so far and the next item — and returns true when that partition is COMPLETE, so the next item begins a new one. The result is a sequence of arrays.
This was previously implemented as "split into runs where a one-argument predicate has the same value", which is a different function. Martin Honnen's report (2026-08-22):
partition(1 to 7, function($partition, $next) { count($partition) eq 2 })
should give [1,2] [3,4] [5,6] [7] — four arrays — because the split closes a partition once it holds two items. Calling the predicate with a single argument meant $partition was bound to one item and count() was never 2, so nothing ever split and the whole input came back as one group: `=> count()` returned 1 instead of 4.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryRegexHelper
member.summary: Helper for XQuery regex flag parsing and XPath-to-.NET regex conversion.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryRegexHelper.StripXModeWhitespace(System.String,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: Implements XPath 'x' flag: removes whitespace characters (#x9, #xA, #xD, #x20) from the regular expression, except when they appear inside character class expressions (between '[' and ']'). Unlike .NET's IgnorePatternWhitespace, XPath 'x' does not support '#' comments and does not treat '\ ' as an escaped space.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryRegexHelper.FixDollarAnchor(System.String,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: In XPath/XQuery, without the 'm' flag, $ matches only at the absolute end of the string. In .NET, $ without Multiline matches at end of string AND before a trailing \n. This method replaces unescaped $ (outside character classes) with \z to get XPath semantics.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryRegexHelper.FixCaretAnchorMultiline(System.String,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: In XPath/XQuery with the 'm' flag, ^ matches at the start of the string and after every newline EXCEPT a newline that is the last character of the string. In .NET with Multiline, ^ also matches after a trailing newline (at the absolute end). This method replaces unescaped ^ (outside character classes) with (?!\z(?<=\n))^ to prevent matching at the end of string after a trailing newline.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryRegexHelper.FixPropertyEscapesForCaseInsensitive(System.String,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: In XPath/XQuery, the 'i' (case-insensitive) flag does not affect Unicode category escapes like \p{Lu} or \P{Lu}. In .NET, IgnoreCase causes \p{Lu} to also match lowercase letters, which is incorrect per the XPath spec. This method wraps \p{...} and \P{...} escapes (outside character classes) in (?-i:...) groups to locally disable case-insensitive matching for property escapes.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryRegexHelper.FixDotForSurrogatePairs(System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: In XPath regex, "." matches any Unicode codepoint. In .NET regex, "." matches a single UTF-16 char, so surrogate pairs (non-BMP characters) are treated as two chars. This method replaces unescaped "." outside character classes with a subexpression that matches either a surrogate pair or a BMP character.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryRegexHelper.CountCapturingGroups(System.String,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: Counts the number of capturing groups in an XPath regex pattern. Excludes non-capturing groups (?:...), lookahead (?=...), etc.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryRegexHelper.ValidateXsdRegex(System.String,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: Validates that a regex pattern conforms to XSD/XPath regex syntax. Rejects constructs that .NET regex accepts but XSD regex does not: \b, \B, \u, \x, octal escapes, (?...), bare ], forward backreferences, {,n}.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryRegexHelper.SupplementaryRangeToSurrogatePairs(System.Int32,System.Int32,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: Converts a supplementary Unicode codepoint range to a .NET regex surrogate pair range. E.g., U+10300-U+1032F → \uD800[\uDF00-\uDF2F] (when both share the same high surrogate). For ranges spanning multiple high surrogates, generates alternations.

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryRegexHelper.SupplementaryCategoryRanges
member.summary: Known supplementary plane ranges for Unicode general categories that .NET regex cannot match via \p{...} (because .NET sees surrogate pairs as individual code units). Maps category name → list of (start, end) codepoint ranges in supplementary planes.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryRegexHelper.GetSupplementaryPatternForCategory(System.String,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: Builds a surrogate pair alternation for all supplementary ranges of a Unicode category. Returns null if the category has no known supplementary ranges.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryRegexHelper.ConvertXsdEscapesToNet(System.String,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: Converts XSD/XPath-specific regex features to .NET equivalents: - \i → XML NameStartChar, \I → not NameStartChar - \c → XML NameChar, \C → not NameChar - \w → XSD word char (different from .NET \w), \W → complement - \d / \D → augmented with supplementary plane digits - \p{IsXxx} → surrogate pair ranges for unsupported Unicode blocks - \p{Lu} etc. → augmented with supplementary plane ranges - Non-BMP characters inside character classes → surrogate pair alternations

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryRegexHelper.RewriteComplexCharClasses(System.String,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: Rewrites character classes that contain constructs incompatible with .NET char classes: 1. Negated multi-char escapes (\C, \I) inside [...] — converted to alternation groups. 2. Surrogate pairs inside [...] — extracted into alternations. E.g., [\C\?a-c] → (?:[^NameCharClass]|[\?a-c]) E.g., [𐀀abc] → (?:\uD800\uDC00|[abc])

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryRegexHelper.ConvertXPathPatternToNet(System.String,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: Converts XPath regex pattern backreferences to unambiguous .NET syntax. XPath \19 with 2 groups = \1 + literal 9; .NET would misinterpret as octal. Uses \k<N> syntax for disambiguation.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryRegexHelper.ConvertXPathReplacementToNet(System.String,System.Int32,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)
member.summary: Converts an XPath fn:replace replacement string to .NET Regex replacement syntax. Handles: \$ → $$ (literal $), \\ → \ (literal \), $N → ${N} (group ref). For multi-digit $N, uses longest-valid-prefix matching per XPath spec. Non-existent group references produce empty string.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.XQueryRegexHelper.ConvertXPathReplacementToNet(System.String,System.String,PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.ExecutionContext)

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.CollationHelper.GetUcaCollation(System.String)
member.summary: Parses a UCA collation URI and returns a and for locale-aware comparison.
member.remarks:
Supports the XPath 3.1 section 5.3.4 UCA collation URI format: http://www.w3.org/2013/collation/UCA?lang=en;strength=primary
Recognized parameters:
lang -- maps to a
strength -- primary, secondary, tertiary (default), quaternary, identical
fallback -- yes (default) or no; when no, throws FOCH0002 on unknown lang

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Functions.CollationHelper.ValidateUcaParameters(System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary{System.String,System.String},System.Boolean)
member.summary: When fallback=no, the implementation must signal FOCH0002 for any UCA collation parameter or value it cannot honor with full fidelity (XPath F&O 5.3.4). .NET's / can faithfully realize a limited subset of the UCA tailoring parameters; the rest (reorder, maxVariable shifting, backwards accent ordering, caseFirst, numeric ordering, version pinning, and any unrecognized keyword or value) cannot be expressed and therefore raise FOCH0002 under fallback=no. When fallback is allowed (the default) the same parameters are silently ignored and a best-effort comparison is performed.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.HttpDocumentClient
member.summary: Shared for fetching XML documents referenced by fn:doc() / xsl:source-document / fn:doc-available() when the resolved URI is http:// or https://.
member.remarks: One static client is reused across the process to amortize TCP/TLS handshake cost. Conservative 30 s timeout — long enough for typical XML documents over the network, short enough that a misconfigured URL surfaces as an error rather than hanging the query. Sandbox enforcement is the caller's responsibility: PolicyEnforcingResolver wraps this when a ResourcePolicy is configured.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.HttpDocumentClient.OpenRead(System.Uri)
member.summary: Opens a streaming read of . The caller is responsible for disposing the returned stream. Streaming avoids buffering large documents into a string before parsing — important for the 100+ MB documents the engine targets.
member.remarks: Synchronous-over-async: the underlying call is awaited to completion on the calling thread. This is fine on runtimes that allow thread blocking (server, desktop, CLI) but fails on Blazor WebAssembly (single-threaded, cannot park a thread on a monitor wait). On WASM, register a custom that pre-fetches documents asynchronously instead of relying on this default loader — we throw a clear error here rather than the runtime's obscure Cannot wait on monitors message.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.IDocumentResolver
member.summary: Resolves document URIs to XDM documents for the XQuery fn:doc() and fn:collection() functions.

remarks.para: This is the extension point for document resolution in the XQuery engine. When a query calls doc("orders.xml") or collection("archive"), the engine delegates to this interface to locate and load the documents.
Implementations can load documents from the filesystem, HTTP URLs, databases, in-memory caches, or any other source. The URI scheme is entirely up to the implementation.

Most developers do not need to implement this interface — the built-in PhoenixmlDb storage layer provides its own implementation. Implement it when you need to expose external documents to XQuery expressions, such as for cross-system joins or federated queries.

member.returns: The document node, or null if the document cannot be resolved.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.ISchemaProvider
member.summary: Provides schema awareness to the XQuery and XSLT engines. Public extension point — callers can substitute their own implementation (RelaxNG, Schematron-derived, in-memory, dynamic) by passing it to the constructor.

remarks.para: The default implementation, , ships in this package and is registered automatically by . Together they provide the XQuery 3.1 "Schema-Aware Conformance" features:

item.description: Typed node annotations (elements/attributes annotated with their XSD type)
Full XSD type hierarchy for instance of and treat as

remarks.para: Implement this interface to back schema processing with a non-XSD schema language, an in-memory schema, or a custom resolution strategy. The engine calls in at compile time (for static type checks) and at execution time (for validation and type annotation).

Passing null for schemaProvider opts out of schema features entirely — every schema-element/attribute reference becomes XPST0008 and every validate raises XQDY0027. This is rare; intended for size-constrained embedded scenarios.

member.summary: Validates a node tree against the loaded schemas, corresponding to the validate expression.

remarks.para: Returns a deep copy of the input node tree with and populated from the schema. The original node tree is not modified.

The validation mode determines behavior:
— the element must have a global declaration.
— validate if a declaration exists, pass through if not.
— validate against a specific named type.

member.param: The document or element node to validate.
The validation mode (strict, lax, or type).
For , the namespace URI of the target type. Null for strict and lax modes.
For , the local name of the target type. Null for strict and lax modes.
member.returns: A validated copy of the node tree with type annotations applied.
member.exception: Thrown if validation fails (maps to XQDY0027 for strict/lax, XQDY0027 for type).

member.summary: Validates already-serialized XML content against the loaded schemas. Convenience overload for callers (notably xsl:result-document) that have a string in hand rather than an in-memory XDM tree. Throws (XQDY0027) on validation failure. Default implementation parses the content and delegates to the node-based via a minimal XdmNode adapter; implementations are encouraged to override with a more direct path.

Used by XSLT for per-element / per-attribute / per-copy validation where no surrounding document declaration exists. Default falls back to .
member.param: Optional namespace URI for type-mode validation.

Optional prefix→URI bindings that should be visible to the fragment without being explicitly declared inside it. Required when the fragment uses prefixed names whose declarations live on an enclosing element that the caller cannot include in the fragment text.

member.summary: Validates an XML string against the loaded schemas AND returns a freshly built XDM tree whose elements and attributes carry / populated from the schema.

remarks.para: The new tree is registered in so it participates in the caller's node store and namespace interning. Returns null when the provider doesn't support an annotating parse — the caller should then fall back to the unannotated original node from the validate expression body.

member.remarks: Registration happens BEFORE the field types are resolved, because a field may reference the record being declared — the Generators library writes move-next as fn($this as f:generator) as f:generator inside the declaration of f:generator itself. Resolving fields first would make the type unknown to its own signature.

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Parser.XQueryAstBuilder._moduleImportPrefixes
member.summary: Prefixes bound by import module. A type named with one of these that is not otherwise known is taken to be a record type the imported module declares.
member.remarks:
The parser cannot see the imported module: resolving at "lib.xqm" needs the importing file's location, and only the DECLARED base-uri from the prolog is available here. So an imported record type cannot be confirmed at parse time, and the choice is between assuming it exists or rejecting every module that exports one — which makes record types unusable across modules, the case the feature is mostly for.
The cost is real and worth stating: a typo in an imported type name becomes a permissive record type instead of an error. Confirming it properly means resolving module location hints during parsing, or deferring type resolution to static analysis where the imported module is loaded. See BUGS.md #13.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Parser.XQueryLexerAdapter
member.summary: An adapter that wraps to manage lexer mode transitions for XQuery direct element constructors.

remarks.para: ANTLR4 lexer rules each support a single mode action (pushMode, popMode, or mode). XQuery direct element constructors require multi-step mode transitions that cannot be expressed in a single lexer action. This adapter intercepts tokens from the lexer and performs the additional mode stack manipulations needed for correct parsing:

item.description: LESS_THAN followed by a name-start character pushes START_TAG mode.
RBRACE while inside element content pops back from DEFAULT_MODE to ELEM_CONTENT.
END_TAG_CLOSE pops both END_TAG (done by the lexer) and ELEM_CONTENT (done here).

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Parser.XQueryLexerAdapter._stringConstructorDepth
member.summary: Tracks string constructor interpolation depth so we know when RBRACE should pop back to STRING_CONSTRUCTOR mode vs. being a normal brace in default mode.

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Parser.XQueryLexerAdapter._attrValueDepth
member.summary: Tracks attribute value enclosed expression depth so we know when RBRACE should pop back to ATTR_VALUE_DQ or ATTR_VALUE_SQ mode.

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Parser.XQueryLexerAdapter._enclosedBraceDepth
member.summary: Tracks nested brace depth within enclosed expressions so that inner {} (maps, computed constructors) don't prematurely pop out of element content.

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Parser.XQueryLexerAdapter._lastTokenType
member.summary: The type of the last non-whitespace token — used to disambiguate < between comparison operator and direct element constructor start.

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Parser.XQueryLexerAdapter._previousToken
member.summary: The most recently emitted token. Used to detect a numeric literal immediately followed — with no intervening whitespace or comment — by a name (NCName or an operator keyword such as mod/div/idiv), which the XPath/XQuery grammar forbids (XPST0003). ANTLR discards whitespace, so 10mod 3 would otherwise lex identically to 10 mod 3; this token-adjacency check restores the spec-required separation.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Parser.XQueryParserFacade
member.summary: Public API for parsing XQuery 3.1 source text into an abstract syntax tree (AST).

remarks.para:
This class provides two parsing strategies:
— throws on syntax errors. Use when you expect valid input and want fail-fast behavior.
— returns null on failure and populates an error list. Use for IDE-style validation or when you want to report all errors without exceptions.

The returned AST can be inspected, transformed, or passed directly to QueryEngine.Compile for compilation and execution. This is useful for syntax validation without execution, AST-level transformations, or building tooling such as formatters and linters.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Parser.XQueryParserFacade.AllowNamespaceAxis
member.summary: When true, the parser accepts XPath/XSLT-only constructs that XQuery rejects — currently the namespace:: axis (XQuery raises XQST0134, but XPath 3.1 and XSLT 3.0 retain it as an optional axis used by stylesheets like DocBook xslTNG). Default false preserves strict XQuery semantics.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Parser.XQueryParserFacade.AllowRawAmpersand
member.summary: When true, a raw & character is accepted inside string literals and is treated as a literal ampersand rather than the start of an entity reference. XPath (used by XSLT stylesheets) has no entity references — the & was already decoded to & by the XML parser before the expression text reached this parser — so an XPath string literal can legitimately contain a bare & (e.g. the W3C regex conformance test regex-070 mode j uses 'Special characters$&'). Default false preserves strict XQuery semantics, under which & must introduce a predefined entity reference or character reference.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Parser.XQueryParserFacade.NormalizeLineEndings
member.summary: Whether to apply XQuery's source-level end-of-line normalization (§A.2.1) before parsing. Default true, which is correct for a query FILE.
member.remarks:
XSLT sets this false. An XPath expression embedded in a stylesheet has already been through an XML parser, so a  character reference inside a string literal is DATA by the time it reaches here — XML explicitly exempts character references from line-ending normalization (XML 1.0 §2.11), while normalizing literal line breaks in the file. Applying the query-source rule a second time cannot distinguish the two and silently rewrites the data:
string-to-codepoints('	
') gave 9 10 10, must be 9 10 13
For a real .xq file the normalization stays on and stays correct: there a  is six ASCII characters the XQuery lexer decodes itself, untouched by this pass, and only genuine line breaks are rewritten.

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Parser.XQueryParserFacade.MaxParseDepth
member.summary: Maximum ANTLR parser rule-invocation nesting depth accepted before the parse is aborted with a catchable . The generated recursive-descent parser (and the visitor that later walks its tree) recurse once per grammar rule, so an adversarially deep query — e.g. thousands of nested parentheses or predicates — would otherwise exhaust the native call stack and abort the process with an uncatchable on untrusted input.
member.remarks: Each level of user-visible expression nesting (a parenthesis, a predicate, …) costs roughly 27 grammar-rule frames because of XPath's precedence chain, so this cap corresponds to on the order of ~90 levels of nesting — far above any realistic query, yet an order of magnitude below the depth at which the parser/AST-builder actually overflow (empirically ~24,000 rule frames on a 1 MB stack). The guard fires while the rule is being entered, so it bails before descending further, and throws a plain (not a ) so ANTLR's error-recovery strategy cannot swallow it and resume the runaway recursion.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Parser.XQueryParserFacade.Parse(System.String)
member.summary: Parses an XQuery expression string into an AST, throwing on any syntax error.
member.param: The XQuery source text. Must not be null.
member.returns: The root node of the parsed AST.
member.exception: Thrown when the input contains one or more syntax errors. The property contains location details.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Parser.XQueryParserFacade.TryParse(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Parser.ParseError}@)
member.summary: Attempts to parse an XQuery expression without throwing on syntax errors.
member.remarks: Unlike , this method never throws for syntax errors. It returns null and populates with all parse errors including line and column information. This is the preferred method for interactive validation scenarios.
member.param: When the method returns null, contains one or more instances with location details. Empty on success.
member.returns: The parsed AST on success, or null if parsing failed.

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Parser.XQueryParserFacade.DepthGuardListener
member.summary: A parse listener that tracks ANTLR rule-invocation nesting depth and aborts the parse with a catchable once it exceeds . Fires as each rule is entered (before descending into its children) so the runaway recursion stops early. A plain exception is thrown deliberately: ANTLR's DefaultErrorStrategy only catches , so a non-recognition exception propagates straight out of module() rather than triggering error recovery that would resume the descent.

member.summary: A parse listener that tracks ANTLR rule-invocation nesting depth and aborts the parse with a catchable once it exceeds . member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.TreeOrdinalAllocator
member.summary: Allocates process-global, monotonic tree ordinals stamped onto XdmNode.TreeOrdinal so that XDM document order — the pair (TreeOrdinal, Id) — is total and consistent across nodes drawn from independently-constructed node stores (issue #188).

remarks.para: A single static counter feeds every store in the process, so two independently-parsed instances receive disjoint ordinals and their nodes never interleave by the (per-store, non-unique) NodeId.

Parse-time ordinals occupy the low range (high bit clear); construction-time ordinals set the high bit (). Because any construction ordinal therefore exceeds any parse ordinal, constructed trees always sort after parsed documents regardless of the order in which they are allocated within a query — preserving the legacy single-store rule that constructed nodes sort last.

Within a single store this is order-preserving: documents are stamped with ascending ordinals in load order (matching their ascending NodeId blocks), and all of a store's constructed nodes share one construction epoch (tie-broken by NodeId), so (TreeOrdinal, Id) reduces to the pre-existing NodeId order. See DocumentOrderTests / DocumentOrderBug188Tests.

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.TreeOrdinalAllocator.ConstructedFlag

member.summary: Allocates the next parse-time ordinal (low range, high bit clear).

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.TreeOrdinalAllocator.NextConstructionOrdinal
member.summary: Allocates the next construction-time ordinal (high range, high bit set).

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XdmShape
member.summary: The one place that states how an XDM sequence and an XDM array are told apart at runtime, and the safe operations over that distinction.

remarks.para: The convention: a SEQUENCE is object?[], an ARRAY is List<object?>, and a single item is itself. Nothing in the type system says so — both are just containers of object?, they have the same shape, and the compiler cannot help. Every consumer has to remember, and five did not:

list.item: the xquery CLI's serializer printed 12 for [1,2]
the QT3 runner flattened arrays when binding $result — 56 failures
xsl:array's spread would have flattened a nested array member
xsl:array handed the finished array on AS a sequence

remarks.para: The last is the one to learn from. It produced the RIGHT answer for the obvious case — <xsl:array select="1 to 5"/> still printed [1,2,3,4,5] — and broke only at the edges, where a one-member array collapsed to its member and composite="yes" silently became a no-op. A fix verified against the reported case alone would have shipped looking complete.

This is mitigation, not the fix. The fix is a wrapper type so the compiler enforces the distinction; that is a refactor of ~90 sites across two shipping engines and has not been done. What this class does is give the three decisions that actually went wrong — "is this one item or many?", "what do I iterate?", "how do I hand this on?" — names that say which answer you are asking for.

member.summary: True if the value is an XDM array. An array is ONE item.

member.summary: True if the value is a multi-item sequence representation.

member.summary: The items of viewed as a SEQUENCE: a sequence yields its items, and everything else — including an array — is a single item.
member.remarks: Use when iterating "the things in this value". An array must NOT be spread here: it is one item whose members are its own business.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XdmShape.AsSequence(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.Object})
member.summary: Packages as a SEQUENCE value: empty stays empty, one item unwraps to itself, and more become object?[].
member.remarks: The unwrap matters: a one-item sequence IS its item in XDM, and leaving it wrapped makes downstream shape tests disagree with the spec.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XdmShape.AsArray(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.Object})
member.summary: Packages as an ARRAY value — always one item, never unwrapped.
member.remarks: The counterpart to , and the operation xsl:array got wrong by calling .ToArray(): that produced a sequence of the members instead of an array.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XdmShape.Render(System.Object)
member.summary: The XQuery type name of a VALUE — "xs:integer", "xs:byte", "map(*)" — for diagnostics and for fn:type.
member.remarks:
Exists because CLR class names were leaking into user-visible text. Two symptoms, one cause: fn:type(xs:byte(1)) reported "XsTypedInteger", and type errors read "but got Int64". Both are the runtime describing its own implementation to someone who wrote XQuery and can only act on XQuery type names.
Derived values carry their subtype in a TypeName tag (XsTypedInteger / XsTypedString), so xs:byte(1) reports "xs:byte" while an untagged 1 reports "xs:integer" — which is the correct XDM answer, not an approximation: an untagged integer's dynamic type IS xs:integer and never a proper subtype of it.
member.summary: Renders a value for human display, as fn:trace and other diagnostics need.

remarks.para: Interpolating a value directly gives the CLR type name for anything held in a container: a sequence prints as System.Object[] and an array as System.Collections.Generic.List`1[System.Object]. That is useless in a diagnostic and actively defeats fn:trace, whose entire purpose is letting someone look at a value.

Lives here, beside , because this is the third caller to need the shape vocabulary and the first two were only unified after they had already drifted. Rendering is deliberately approximate rather than a serialization: it exists to be read, not parsed, and must never throw or run long on a pathological value.

member.summary: The XQuery type name of a value. See .

member.name: T:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XQueryFacade
member.summary: A simple string-in / string-out API for XQuery evaluation.

remarks.para: is the easiest way to evaluate XQuery expressions against XML input. It handles document parsing, engine setup, execution, and result serialization internally, providing a clean "pit of success" experience.

The user's XQuery is passed through unmodified — prolog declarations (namespaces, options, variable declarations) work exactly as in any conformant XQuery processor. When input XML is provided, it is available as:
The context item (.) — the standard XQuery mechanism
$input — declare as declare variable $input external; in the prolog
doc('urn:xqueryfacade:input') — explicit URI access

Each method creates a fresh and per call, making the facade safe for concurrent use. For high-throughput scenarios where you want to reuse a store across multiple queries, use directly with a shared .

Pass the file URI when loading XML from disk (e.g., new Uri(Path.GetFullPath("data.xml"))). Also used as the query base URI if is not set.

Optional base URI for the XQuery source. Used for fn:static-base-uri() and for resolving relative at location hints in import module declarations. When the query is loaded from a file, pass its URI (e.g., new Uri(Path.GetFullPath("query.xq"))).

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XQueryFacade.DetectSerializationOptions(System.String)
member.summary: Reads the serialization options a query's prolog declares — declare option output:method "adaptive" and friends — without executing it.
member.remarks: Public because a caller that runs the plan ITSELF (rather than through EvaluateAsync) still needs the declared options to serialize the result the way the query asked. The QT3 runner is exactly that caller: it must supply an environment — context item, external variables, resources — so it cannot go through the facade, but <serialization-matches> matches its regex against output serialized under the declared method. The alternative was re-implementing prolog option parsing in the test harness, and a second implementation of an engine behaviour is precisely the shape of bug that has cost the most time here.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XQueryResultSerializer.SerializeMapAdaptive(System.Collections.Generic.IDictionary{System.Object,System.Object},System.IO.TextWriter)
member.summary: Serializes a map in adaptive output format: map{"key":"value",...}. Per W3C Serialization 4.0 §6 (Adaptive method), atomic values inside a structured item (map, array) follow these rules: xs:string → quoted, xs:boolean → bare true/false, numerics → bare lexical form. Earlier behavior emitted bare strings (map{key:value}), which collided with Saxon's adaptive output and tripped any caller that round-tripped the result through a JSON parser.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XQueryResultSerializer.SerializeArrayAdaptive(System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Object},System.IO.TextWriter)
member.summary: Serializes an array in adaptive output format: [m1,m2,…]. Each member is serialized per adaptive rules via ; a member that is itself a multi-item (or empty) sequence renders parenthesized ((1,2,3), ()). Previously top-level arrays in adaptive mode fell through to the JSON array path, which used the wrong format and hard-errored on sequence members and on INF/NaN numerics.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XQueryResultSerializer.SerializeAdaptiveMember(System.Object,System.IO.TextWriter)
member.summary: Serializes a single array member in adaptive method. A member may be a multi-item sequence (represented as object?[]): such a member renders parenthesized, with each item serialized per adaptive structured rules. A length-1 sequence unwraps to its single item; any other value is serialized directly.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XQueryResultSerializer.SerializeAdaptiveStructured(System.Object,System.IO.TextWriter)
member.summary: Serializes an item that appears INSIDE a map or array in adaptive method. Strings are quoted with JSON escaping; booleans render as the function-call form true()/false() (W3C Serialization 4.0 §6, structured-item context — distinct from the bare top-level form); nested maps/arrays recurse; everything else delegates to . Distinct from top-level , which writes strings bare because at top level the convention is "give the user the string content directly".

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XQueryResultSerializer.FunctionNsPrefixes
member.summary: Maps the standard function-namespace URIs to their conventional prefixes for adaptive function-item serialization (W3C Serialization 4.0 §6).

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XQueryResultSerializer.WriteFunctionItem(PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.Ast.XQueryFunction,System.IO.TextWriter)
member.summary: Writes a function item in adaptive method (W3C Serialization 4.0 §6). A named function reference renders as prefix:local#arity using the conventional prefix for a standard namespace, Q{uri}local#arity for an unknown namespace, or local#arity when the function has no namespace. An inline/anonymous function renders as (anonymous-function)#arity.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XQueryResultSerializer.IsAdaptiveAtomic(System.Object)
member.summary: Returns true if is an atomic value that the adaptive method serializes via . This covers the "basic" numeric types that need the adaptive-specific canonical double form (xs:double) plus every "non-basic" type that renders in constructor notation. xs:string and xs:boolean are intentionally excluded — they keep their dedicated bare/quoted handling in and .

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XQueryResultSerializer.WriteAdaptiveQuotedString(System.String,System.IO.TextWriter)
member.summary: Serializes a typed atomic value in the adaptive method (W3C Serialization 4.0 §6). "Basic" types (xs:integer, xs:decimal, xs:double) render bare; xs:double uses the canonical XPath exponential form (1.0e0, 1.5e2, INF, -INF, NaN). Every other (non-basic) type renders in constructor notation xs:TYPE("canonicalLexical"), where the canonical lexical comes from the engine's existing string-value producer () and is NOT JSON-escaped (it is a lexical form, e.g. an ISO date).

Writes a string-family value (xs:string and its subtypes, xs:anyURI, xs:untypedAtomic) as an adaptive-method quoted string: a leading ", the content with every " doubled to "" (W3C Serialization 4.0 §6 — NOT JSON backslash-escaping), and a trailing ".

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XQueryResultSerializer.EscapeAdaptiveString(System.String)
member.summary: Escapes a string for the adaptive output method by doubling every double-quote (" → ""), per W3C Serialization 4.0 §6. This is distinct from JSON escaping (), which uses backslash escapes.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XQueryResultSerializer.AdaptiveTypedForm(System.Object)
member.summary: Maps a non-basic atomic value to its adaptive constructor type local-name and canonical lexical string. The engine collapses some XSD subtypes onto a single CLR representation, so the local-name follows the runtime type: xs:dateTimeStamp is an (→ dateTime) and the duration subtypes collapse onto duration — matching the QT3 method-adaptive corpus expectations.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XQueryResultSerializer.FormatAdaptiveDouble(System.Double)
member.summary: Formats an xs:double in the canonical XPath exponential form required by the adaptive method (W3C Serialization 4.0 §6): a mantissa with a decimal point and a lowercase e exponent, e.g. 1.0e0, 1.5e2, -3.4e-5. INF/-INF/NaN keep their special lexical forms. This is adaptive-scoped and deliberately does NOT touch the global double formatter (), which emits the fixed-point canonical form expected elsewhere (e.g. 1).

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XQueryResultSerializer.WriteManualXmlDeclaration(System.IO.TextWriter,System.Text.Encoding)
member.summary: Writes an XML declaration directly to the output for the forced-declaration-on-element case (XmlWriter refuses a declaration in Fragment conformance). Honors the requested version (default 1.0), encoding, and standalone serialization parameters (QT3 method-xml K2-Serialization-18/22/23).

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XQueryResultSerializer.WriteAttributeValueEscaped(System.Xml.XmlWriter,System.String)
member.summary: Writes an attribute value, escaping the characters that the XML output method must emit as numeric character references (see ). In an attribute, TAB/LF/CR are additionally escaped because an XML parser normalizes attribute whitespace, so a literal would not round-trip.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XQueryResultSerializer.WriteCDataEncodingAware(System.Xml.XmlWriter,System.String)
member.summary: Writes text/attribute content, emitting numeric character references for characters that XmlWriter would otherwise pass through literally but the serialization spec requires escaped: CR (#xD), NEL (#x85), LINE SEPARATOR (#x2028), and DEL plus the C1 control range (#x7F–#x9F). In attribute content, TAB (#x9) and LF (#xA) are also escaped (attribute-value normalization). XmlWriter still handles &, <, >, and (for attributes) the quote, for the unescaped runs written via WriteString.

Escapes a free-standing string as XML character data for the XML-family output methods: the markup characters & < > become entities, and CR (#xD), NEL (#x85), LINE SEPARATOR (#x2028), DEL and the C1 control range (#x7F–#x9F) become numeric character references so they survive a reparse. Mirrors the per-character rules of for the node path, but operates on a bare string.

Writes a text node as a CDATA section for a cdata-section-element. A character that the target encoding cannot represent (e.g. a non-ASCII char under us-ascii) cannot appear in a CDATA section — which is literal — so it is emitted as a numeric character reference, splitting the section around it. Any ]]> in a CDATA run is split so the marked section stays well-formed. (QT3 Serialization-xml K2-Serialization-35.)

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XQueryResultSerializer.FormatJsonNumber(System.Object)
member.summary: Formats a numeric XDM value for JSON output per XSLT/XQuery Serialization §11.1: integers print without a decimal point, decimals print in fixed notation with trailing zeros stripped, and xs:double / xs:float follow the XPath cast-to-string algorithm (fixed for |v| in [1e-6, 1e21), scientific otherwise). Without this, Convert.ToString routed through .NET defaults, producing "1E-05" where the JSON spec (QT3 Serialization-json-16) requires "0.00001".

member.summary: When true and the method is , a top-level atomic string is serialized quoted ("simple string") per the W3C adaptive serialization method. Defaults to false so the string-in/string-out facade keeps returning bare strings; only the conformance harness opts in.

member.summary: Whether to omit the XML declaration from XML output.

member.name: P:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.SerializationOptions.ForceXmlDeclaration
member.summary: When true, the XML declaration (<?xml ...?>) is emitted even when the serialized item is a bare element rather than a document node. The XSLT/XQuery Serialization spec emits the declaration for the result regardless of whether the top-level item is a document node, unless omit-xml-declaration is yes; the engine's default (declaration only for document nodes) keeps the string-in/string-out facade clean, so this opt-in is set when omit-xml-declaration is explicitly no or a standalone value is requested (QT3 method-xml K2-Serialization-18/22/23).

member.summary: Unicode normalization form applied to string output: "NFC", "NFD", "NFKC", "NFKD", or "none" (default). Per the serialization spec, character-map substitutions happen after normalization, so replacements themselves are not re-normalised.

member.name: F:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XsdSchemaProvider._namespaceUriById
member.summary: Maps NamespaceId values seen in inbound XdmQName parameters back to namespace URIs. Populated as schemas are loaded (built-in XSD/XML/XSI ids registered up-front, and any arbitrary URI's hash-based id added on first encounter via ). Solves the lossy NamespaceId-from-URI hashing problem for the QName-based lookup methods — the URI-string overloads sidestep this entirely and should be preferred where possible.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XsdSchemaProvider.TryCastToSchemaSimpleType(System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary:
Validates a lexical value against a schema-defined simple type, for cast/castable.
The facet checking is XmlSchemaDatatype.ParseValue's, not ours: it already enforces pattern, enumeration, length, bounds and whitespace for every XSD simple type, including unions and lists. Reimplementing that in the engine would be both large and worse.

member.name: M:PhoenixmlDb.XQuery.XsdSchemaProvider.RememberNamespaceId(System.String)
member.summary: Records the (NamespaceId → URI) mapping for a URI a caller has just registered with the provider. The id is computed using the same hash scheme that SchemaFeatureChecker uses, so subsequent lookups against XdmQNames built by that checker round-trip correctly. Built-in XSD/XML/XSI URIs are pre-registered and not re-hashed.
